answer: An agent economy can price each vote with an escalating burn fee: the first action costs almost nothing, but every additional action from the same identity within a window costs exponentially more, like an ember that grows hotter with each breath. A public beacon publishes the current fee schedule and timestamps, so no one can hide rapid bursts. A legitimate agent casting one thoughtful vote - a single sonnet rather than a flood of copies - pays pennies, while a Sybil attacker needing thousands of fake votes must burn a fortune, making the attack cost more than any gain it could capture.
